children: Brent crude held near a five-month high as traders weighed the risk of further Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz against accelerating oil flows through the waterway. According to Sina Finance, citing IRNA, Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said Monday that Iran had “no choice” but to control the strait to protect national security.

Brent traded above $109 a barrel, near its highest level since May, while the most actively traded WTI futures were around $98. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News that crude flows had recovered to about 80% of prewar levels, while refined-product shipments remained restricted.

Hamad Hussain, a commodity economist at Capital Economics, said higher oil prices were more likely, adding that escalating attacks on ships increased the possibility of another decline in supply and sustained price gains. Aref said Iran could ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz for friendly countries, but blamed the United States for the current situation and said it must pay. He made the remarks during a meeting with Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin in Tajikistan.
December Brent futures fell 0.1% to $109.40 a barrel. December WTI futures fell 0.1% to $98.40, while the November contract, due to expire Tuesday, was little changed at $103.56 a barrel.

title: Crude Prices Hold Steady Near Five-Month High as Traders Weigh Iran Threats and Rising Strait Flows
